ghs.assessment: The Japanese narrates the transition of waking up. The English gives a past state of already being awake.

rows.jp: 机に突っ伏して寝ていたらしい。
rows.en: Apparently, I'd fallen asleep facedown on the desk.

ghs.en: Seems I had fallen prostrate on the desk and slept.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says he apparently fell asleep slumped face-down over the desk. 'Fallen prostrate' suggests a full-body posture and coordinating it with 'slept' obscures the single event.

highlights.text: fallen prostrate on the desk and slept

rows.en: A dream that should have felt nostalgic.

ghs.en: a dream that should have been nostalgic.

rows.jp: けど憂鬱な気分になってしまう。
rows.en: But it only leaves me depressed.

ghs.en: But my mood turned to melancholy.

rows.jp: 結局人は、自分のために生きている。
rows.en: In the end, people live for themselves.

ghs.en: In the end, people are living for their own sake.

rows.jp: 人と触れあうことで生じる、様々な欲望の中で。
rows.en: Amid all the desires born of contact with others.

ghs.en: In the midst of so many desires produced by a meeting of touches with other people.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese refers to interacting or coming into contact with other people. The English calques the components into a physically incoherent 'meeting of touches.'

highlights.text: a meeting of touches with other people

rows.jp: 汗ばんだ体を冷やしに、屋上に向かう。
rows.en: I head for the roof to cool off.

ghs.en: To cool down my sweaty body, I head towards the rooftop.
